{{Short description|Theorem in group theory}}
{{distinguish|Law of trichotomy}}

In [[group theory]], the '''trichotomy theorem''' divides the [[finite simple group]]s of [[characteristic 2 type]] and [[rank (group theory)|rank]] at least&nbsp;3 into three classes. It was [[mathematical proof|proved]] by Michael Aschbacher<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Aschbacher |first=Michael |date=October 1981 |title=Finite groups of rank 3. I |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01389061 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |language=en |volume=63 |issue=3 |pages=357–402 |doi=10.1007/BF01389061 |issn=0020-9910|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Aschbacher |first=Michael |date=February 1983 |title=Finite groups of rank 3. II |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01393339 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |language=en |volume=71 |issue=1 |pages=51–163 |doi=10.1007/BF01393339 |issn=0020-9910|url-access=subscription }}</ref> for rank&nbsp;3, and by Gorenstein and Lyons<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gorenstein |first=Daniel |last2=Lyons |first2=Richard |date=1983 |title=The local structure of finite groups of characteristic 2 type |url=http://www.ams.org/memo/0276 |journal=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=42 |issue=276 |pages=0–0 |doi=10.1090/memo/0276 |issn=0065-9266|url-access=subscription }}</ref> for rank at least&nbsp;4. The three classes are [[groups of GF(2) type]] (classified by Timmesfeld and others), groups of "standard type" for some [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] [[prime number|prime]] (classified by the [[Gilman–Griess theorem]] and work by several others), and [[Uniqueness case|groups of uniqueness type]], where Aschbacher proved that there are no [[simple group]]s.
